messages:
Taro Sato: Hey team — I'm leaving Japan next Friday (2024-11-22). Quick Q about final pay: how will my last month's salary and unused PTO be handled? Will tax/social insurance be withheld differently because I'm departing the country? Also curious whether I'll get a Japanese 源泉徴収票 (gensenchoshuhyo) and a US W-2 or just one of them. Thanks.
María (People Ops): @Taro :wave: sorry to see you go — congrats on your next step. We need a couple of details to advise: employment end date, whether you were on payroll in JP as a local employee or working remotely on a US contract, and your current bank for final transfer.
Taro Sato: End date is 2024-11-22 (last working day). I was a local employee in Japan (signed local JP contract, enrolled in shakai hoken). Bank is JP account (SMBC) but would prefer final pay to my US account if possible — will that complicate withholding?
Alex Chen: Hi Taro — because you were a local JP employee, final payroll will run under local payroll rules. PTO is prorated per policy (see handbook section: "Final Pay & PTO") — unused paid leave payout is included in final payrun unless you choose payout at separation. If you move bank accounts cross-border we need an international transfer; that can introduce conversion fees and may delay payment 3-5 business days.
Lisa (Finance): Quick finance note: for social insurance (shakai hoken) contributions, if termination occurs mid-month we typically calculate contributions through your termination month and deduct employer/employee portions on the final paycheck. That can change net. We also check year-to-date tax withholding and may make a final adjustment on the last payroll.
María (People Ops): For forms: because you were on Japan payroll, you'll get a JP 源泉徴収票 for the period you worked in JP. Redwood will also issue a US W-2 for US-sourced compensation if you were on US payroll at any point this tax year — in your case, looks like JP only, so likely only the JP form. If you later need a W-2 for US tax filing, open a ticket and we can confirm.
Taro Sato: OK — thanks. Is there any way to reduce the final month withholding? I had extra tax withheld earlier this year. I don't want to over-withheld.
Alex Chen: There's limited flexibility once payroll is processed. We can review YTD withholding and, if there's an obvious overwithholding, coordinate a refund via payroll adjustment or a direct refund post-close. Please attach your last paystub and any prior tax docs when you open the ticket.
Payroll Bot: [system] Payroll run scheduled: 2024-11-27 03:00 JST. Termination records submitted by 2024-11-24 17:00 JST will be included in that run.
María (People Ops): Action items for you, @Taro: 1) Confirm preferred destination account for final pay (JP or US) 2) Upload a copy of passport exit date if you want expedited non-resident tax handling 3) Approve PTO payout option (payout vs. cashout) in Workday by 2024-11-21.
Taro Sato: I'll keep JP bank for the final run (to avoid transfer delays) and upload passport exit scan today. I'll select payout for PTO in Workday.
Lisa (Finance): One more thing — please confirm whether any employer-sponsored benefits (commuter, gym subsidy) should be prorated or canceled prior to 11/22. If benefits are billed monthly, we'll stop at termination date to avoid recoveries.
María (People Ops): Great. Once you upload the docs I'll create a payroll ticket and tag finance. Expect final paystub posted in the payroll portal ~48 hours after the run completes. If there's any withholding refund needed we'll loop back with timelines.
Taro Sato: Thanks everyone. Appreciate the help — will update when docs are uploaded.
María (People Ops): Thanks @Taro — ping us if anything changes. :thumbsup:
Lisa (Finance): Noted — I'll watch for the payroll ticket and do a preliminary YTD run to estimate net.
Payroll Bot: [system] Ticket created: PAY-76421 by María (People Ops).
